From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Integration & observability follow-up — FintechCo

Hi Alex —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from today's discovery and some concrete next steps so we stay momentum: 

Summary of needs we heard:
- Integration: SDK onboarding (Node/Python), API key + optional OAuth for service accounts, and sample routing policy (latency-first to dedicated pool).
- Features: structured output for tool-calling (function-like JSON outputs), embeddings + reranker for semantic search/ranking, and server-side rerank pipeline.
- Observability: trace IDs propagated from FintechCo's front-end/backend into Redwood requests, explicit logging fields for request_id/trace_id/model/route, and a latency-breakdown header for per-hop metrics (kernel / kv-cache / transport).

Concrete next steps we propose:
1) I'll send a short Integration Checklist + SDK snippets (attached) for your engineers to try a quick smoke test (token generation, a sample call, and trace header propagation).
2) Vivek to propose routing and fallback policy for production (dedicated -> hosted fallback).
3) Schedule a 45-min technical deep dive next Tue (Mar 3) with your infra + our runtime/observability engineers.
4) We'll provide an example reranker using FintechCo's sample embeddings and a small evaluation harness.

Attachments: redwood-integration-checklist.pdf, redwood-observability-snippets.md, MVP-mattersheet.xlsx

Notes on observability (high-level):
- Header: please pass X-Redwood-Trace (trace-id) and X-Redwood-Span (span-id) from your caller. We'll echo these into logs.
- Response header: X-Redwood-Latency: total=120ms;kernel=70ms;kv_cache=20ms;transport=30ms
- Logging fields we recommend: request_id, trace_id, tenant_id, model, route, tokens_in, tokens_out, batch_id, quantization_profile
- We'll include a dashboard sample (latency by route, error rate, tokens per response, avg model latency) in the deep dive.

If this looks good, can you confirm who from FintechCo will join next Tue and whether we should include procurement for licensing conversation?

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0196

Alex —

Great questions. Short answers:
- Trace format: We accept W3C traceparent and also support a simple string in X-Redwood-Trace; if you use W3C we map it into our traces.
- Minimal curl example (smoke test):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDSK-API-KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-Trace: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01' \
  -d '{"model":"rw-instruct-large-v1","input":"Summarize transaction anomalies","structured_output":{"type":"json","schema":{"summary":"string","risk_score":"number"}},"return_trace":true}'

Response will include: a JSON payload (structured_output) and headers: X-Redwood-Trace (echoed), X-Redwood-Latency with per-component breakdown.

I'll attach a longer snippet for Node/Python in redwood-observability-snippets.md. For auth: you can use a service API key for initial pilot; for private deployments/production we recommend mTLS or OAuth service accounts.

We'll plan to cover the reranker template in the deep dive — sample embedding model we typically use is "redwood-embed-2" (dim: 1536) but we'll validate offline with your sample docs.

If helpful, here's a tiny Node example (pseudocode) to send trace header and log response headers: 

// Node snippet
const res = await sdk.generate({ model: 'rw-instruct-large-v1', input: '...'}, { headers: { 'X-Redwood-Trace': traceId } });
console.log(res.headers['x-redwood-latency'], res.headers['x-redwood-trace']);

I'll be on the deep dive and can walk through runtime-level latency breakdowns.

Cheers,
Marissa
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Alex —

Quick note from the runtime/ops side ahead of the deep dive:
- Routing: we'll suggest a policy that evaluates latency SLO and cost. Example rule: route to dedicated pool in us-west for requests with header X-Tenant-Plan: enterprise; otherwise prefer hosted. Fallback: if dedicated latency >150ms or capacity pressure detected, route to hosted compatible model variant.
- Headers & dashboards: we will emit X-Redwood-Latency on all successful responses. For errors we include X-Redwood-Error-Code and X-Redwood-Trace.
- Log schema (JSON line): { request_id, trace_id, tenant_id, model, route, tokens_in, tokens_out, batch_id, kernel_ms, kv_cache_ms, transport_ms, total_ms } (we'll provide concrete examples in the deep dive doc).
- Reranker flow: store embeddings in your vector DB, call Redwood to return top-K candidates + rerank using a light model prompt; we can provide an evaluation harness for precision@10.

I'll bring sample dashboards: latency by route/model, errors by tenant, tokens per request, and a trace view that ties a single request_id to per-kernel timings.

See you Tue.
Vivek
Head of Reliability | Redwood Inference
